newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 19.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - One of the biggest problems facing Czech industry is still payment problems. The total volume of unpaid debts in the business sector is continually growing, according to both the Czech Statistical Bureau and the Industry and Transport Union.

- Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky has presented Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus with reworked material regarding the privatisation of the four big Czech banks, according to CNB spokesman Martin Svehla. The new material defines the bank's plan to privatise Investicni a Postovni Banka more concretely while the plan to merge Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka remains unchanged.

- The majority of the work force and capacity of CKD Horovice and CKD Hradec Kralove will merge to become CKD Motory, a new daughter company of CKD Praha. The change becomes effective December 1. CKD plans to integrate the development, final production and trade of diesel motors.

- Retail store owners posted the largest sales increases in sales so far this year in September. Compared with the same period last year, sales increased by 21.4 percent in nominal terms, according to the Czech Statistics Bureau. One of the reasons for this increase is the current distrust of the banking sphere which leads to less savings and more spending, according to the general director of Ceska Sporitelna, Jaroslav Klapal.

- Average wages are rising by approximately 18 percent, according to the Czech National Bank. The rapid increase of wages is not balanced by developments in the economy and creates higher inflationary pressure.
- CEZ will not know the date that the Temelin nuclear power plant will begin operations until at least this December. Meetings among the major suppliers are still taking place.
- The crown strengthened slightly on the interbank markets in the aftermath of the first round of elections to the Czech senate.

- The development of international crude oil prices are only partially responsible for this year's drastic increase of diesel fuel prices. While crude oil prices have increased by only 20 percent since the beginning of the year, Ceska Rafinerka's prices for diesel fuel have increased by 60 percent.
- The situation at Czech Railways is so strained that a December strike is a real possibility, according to the vice-chairman of the Railway Workers Union, Jiri Kratochvil.

- Both Eurotel and RadioMobil want to offer their customers access to the Internet over their mobile phone network. Currently GSM phone users can hook up to the Internet, but only using SPT Telecom numbers, which can cost up to 12 crowns a minute to connect to.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Over half of the domestic production of sugar is currently under the control of foreign companies.
PRAVO - Pope John Paul II may visit Prague and Hradec Kralove between April 25 to 27, 1997 pending final confirmation from the Vatican. This would be the Pope's third visit to the Czech Republic.
